k: The classic: a too-cheap package on social media, payment by bank transfer only, then the "agent" vanishes — or you land with no hotel booking. <1>Protect yourself:</1> for Umrah, book through <2><3>umrah.nusuk.sa</3></2> (every provider there is licensed by the Ministry of Hajj & Umrah) or an agent whose ministry accreditation you can verify; for Hajj, book only through your country's official Hajj channel; in the UK check ATOL/ABTA protection (in the EU, the insolvency protection every package holiday must carry); pay by credit card, never untraceable transfer; and treat any "guaranteed visa in {1} hours" claim as a red flag.

Unofficial wheelchair pushers may quote one price and demand triple at the end — use the <1>official wheelchair desks</1> inside the Haram or agree a written price first. Street taxis: agree the fare before the door closes, or use Careem/Uber. Money changers: count your riyals at the counter. And the "found gold ring — buy it from me cheap" trick is brass, not gold.

WhatsApp and Facebook messages announcing you won a free Umrah, an iPhone-and-Umrah bundle, or a charity lottery — just pay a small "processing fee" or share your details. No ministry runs lotteries by WhatsApp. Delete, block, and warn the family group.
<1>After ihram, before tawaf:</1> stay in ihram, wait for purity, then perform ghusl, tawaf and sa'i. If bleeding ends in time, nothing is lost.

<1>Before the miqat:</1> enter ihram anyway — ihram does not require purity — and keep up the talbiyah, dhikr and dua. When Aishah (RA) got her period at Sarif, the Prophet ﷺ told her: "Do what all the pilgrims do, except that you do not perform tawaf around the Ka'bah until you are clean" (Bukhari {1}).

<1>If your flight comes before purity</1>, the rulings differ (some scholars permit tawaf with precautions in genuine necessity) — ask a scholar you trust before travelling; do not decide alone at the airport.
<1>No raml</1> (brisk walk) in the first three rounds of tawaf, and <2>no jogging</2> between the green lights in sa'i — walk at a normal pace throughout. Both are sunnah for men only.

<1>On Hajj:</1> everything continues except tawaf (and the sa'i after it); tawaf al-ifadah waits, and the farewell tawaf is waived if you are still bleeding when you leave — on a Hajj journey, see "Hajj for sisters" in the fiqh Q&A.

<1>When men pass close by:</1> Aishah (RA) reported that the women with the Prophet ﷺ in ihram would let their outer garment down from the head over the face while riders passed, then uncover again (Abu Dawud {1}, which al-Albani and others grade weak; a similar practice is reported with a sound chain from women in ihram with Asma bint Abi Bakr, Muwatta Malik). Scholars differ on how far this applies today — many allow a loose cloth draped from the head that does not sit tied on the face; others say the face stays uncovered. Follow the scholar you trust; either way, a tied niqab is not worn in ihram.
A doctor can advise on delaying the period if your dates clash — decide well before you fly.
A husband or mahram may cut for you after he has exited his own ihram.

After sa'i in Umrah — or after the stoning on the {1}th in Hajj — gather your hair and cut about a <1>fingertip's length (≈{2} cm) from the ends</1>. Women never shave: "Shaving is not a duty laid on women; only clipping the hair is incumbent on them" (Abu Dawud {3}).
Agree a <1>family meeting point</1> (a numbered gate) before every prayer — save it in the Hotel & SOS card and it appears on your "I'm lost" page.
Both Harams have designated <1>women's prayer sections</1> — look for the signs and the women's gates; arrive {1}–{2} min before prayer.
Cut somewhere private — in the ladies' area or back at the hotel; the restrictions of ihram stay in force until you cut (in Hajj: until your first release).
Idtiba' (uncovering the right shoulder) is likewise for men only.
Keep the hotel card (name, address, phone) with you; the driver page works offline.
Keep to the calmer outer rings or upper floors if the mataf is crowded; the tawaf is equally valid, and avoiding the crush is better for you.
Ladies' wudu and toilet blocks are separate and signposted around the courtyards.

Most scholars hold that Umrah has no obligatory farewell tawaf (some require it of anyone leaving Makkah, so doing it when you can is safer) — and for a menstruating woman the farewell tawaf is waived even in Hajj (Safiyyah RA, Bukhari {1}).
Pack a small pair of scissors in your checked luggage (hand-luggage rules vary by airline) so you are not depending on anyone.
Phone signal drops inside the Haram — agree a time as well as a place.
Recite the talbiyah in a low voice — loud recitation is the men's sunnah, not yours.
Sa'i follows tawaf, so both wait; dua and dhikr in the Haram courtyards continue.
Sisters travelling in a group: pair up for tawaf and sa'i, and keep the group leader's number on paper as well as in your phone.

The <1>Rawdah</1> in Masjid an-Nabawi has dedicated women's time slots — book them through the same free Nusuk permit (women's section). Salam on the Prophet ﷺ and his two companions is made from the women's side of the chamber.
The <1>ground-floor mataf is mixed</1> and very crowded. Late night to pre-Fajr is calmest; the upper floors are longer but far more comfortable for tawaf in a family group.

There is no special garment for women: your ordinary, loose, modest clothing — <1>in any colour</1> — is your ihram. Two things change once you are in ihram: <2>no niqab and no gloves</2> — the Prophet ﷺ said "the woman in ihram should not wear a niqab or gloves" (Bukhari {1}). The Hanafi school permits gloves, but the majority forbid them, so avoiding them is safer. Socks, hijab pins, a watch, plain jewellery, a bag and an umbrella are all fine.
Use the <1>women-only gates and sections</1> during crowd surges; staff will direct you.

Women are <1>not admitted inside</1> Jannat al-Baqi' in Madinah (nor Jannat al-Mu'alla in Makkah), and the martyrs' graves at Uhud are fenced off for everyone — men and women alike greet them from outside the fence. This is no loss: the sunnah greeting — "As-salamu 'alaykum, people of these dwellings, of the believers and the Muslims…" (Muslim {1}) — is valid from the gate or the fence, and the dua for the dead reaches them wherever you stand. Visit after Fajr or Asr when the men's gates are open and the family can meet at a fixed spot afterwards.

<1>"Follow up between Hajj and Umrah, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows removes the dross of iron, gold and silver."</1> (Tirmidhi {1}). The money you spend on this journey is never a loss.

<1>"One prayer in this masjid of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except al-Masjid al-Haram — and one prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than a hundred thousand prayers elsewhere."</1> (Ibn Majah {1}). One Fajr in the Haram outweighs ~{2} years of prayers. Five daily prayers for a week here is a lifetime of reward — never sleep through a congregation.

<1>"The one who fights in Allah's cause, the Hajj pilgrim and the Umrah pilgrim are the delegation of Allah: He called them and they answered, and they ask of Him and He gives them."</1> (Ibn Majah {1}, graded hasan by al-Albani). Arrive with your dua list ready — you have an audience with the Most Generous Host.

<1>"Whoever performs tawaf around this House seven times and keeps count of it is like one who frees a slave."</1> With every step "a sin is erased and a good deed is recorded" (Tirmidhi {1}). And tawaf is worship you can ONLY do here — fill your trip with it.

Anas (RA) was asked how many Umrahs the Prophet ﷺ performed: <1>"Four — the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, the Umrah of the following year (al-Qada), the Umrah from al-Ji'ranah, and the Umrah with his Hajj."</1> (Bukhari {1}, {2}). He also ordered Aishah's brother to take her to <2>Tan'eem</2> so she could perform an extra Umrah (Bukhari {3}) — the very miqat you can use for a second Umrah today.

Leaving for the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ said of Makkah: <1>"By Allah, you are the best of Allah's land, and the most beloved of Allah's land to Allah. Had I not been driven out of you, I would never have left."</1> (Tirmidhi {1}). The Haram is a sanctuary where even the trees and game are protected — carry its adab everywhere.

The Prophet ﷺ said: <1>"The jihad of the elderly, the young, the weak and women is Hajj and Umrah."</1> (Nasai {1}). And when Aishah (RA) asked if women have jihad, he said: "Jihad in which there is no fighting — Hajj and Umrah." (Ibn Majah {2}). Every drop of sweat in the mataf is counted.

The Prophet ﷺ said: <1>"Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for the sins committed between them, and the accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise."</1> (Bukhari {1}). Whoever performs the pilgrimage without obscenity or wickedness "returns as the day his mother bore him" (Muslim {2}). You come home with a clean slate — guard it.
